question: What is the primary focus of critical care nursing in the ICU?

options.A: Conducting long-term physical therapy and rehabilitation exercises
options.B: Providing continuous monitoring and specialized care for life-threatening problems
options.C: Managing basic daily hygiene and routine oral medication schedules
options.D: Discharging stable patients back to their primary care providers

explanation: Critical care nursing is specifically designed for patients with life-threatening conditions who need close observation and advanced interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h1)

question: What danger is associated with alarm fatigue in a busy ICU?

options.A: Nurses might miss critical changes in a patient's condition due to constant noise
options.B: Equipment batteries drain faster when alarms sound repeatedly
options.C: Patients sleep better because they get used to the background sounds
options.D: Doctors refuse to enter the unit until all monitors are silenced

explanation: When monitors beep constantly for non-emergencies, staff can become desensitized. You're doing great—staying alert to this helps keep patients safe! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE systematic assessment approach?
explanation: In the ABCDE emergency assessment framework, B stands for evaluating the patient's breathing status and chest movement. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient with a head injury has a lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score than before. What does this usually mean?

options.B: Successful adaptation to the ICU environment

explanation: A dropping GCS score means the patient's level of consciousness is worsening. Catching this early lets the team act fast to help them! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of using an arterial line instead of a standard blood pressure cuff?

options.A: It automatically delivers intravenous fluids when pressure drops
options.B: It measures the exact amount of urine produced by the kidneys
options.C: It provides continuous, real-time blood pressure readings
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of infection and bleeding

explanation: An arterial line gives beat-by-beat blood pressure updates, which is super helpful for unstable patients whose numbers change fast. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why are strong drugs like norepinephrine given through a central line instead of a regular vein in the hand or arm?

options.A: To avoid the need for any blood pressure monitoring equipment
options.B: To reduce the total cost of nursing care during the shift
options.C: To prevent severe local tissue damage if the medication leaks out
options.D: To speed up how fast the drug reaches the brain and heart

explanation: These medications can cause severe skin and tissue damage if they leak outside a small peripheral vein. Central lines are much safer for them! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is an easy, key nursing action to help prevent pneumonia in patients on a breathing machine (ventilator)?

options.A: Changing the endotracheal tube every twelve hours
options.B: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all ventilated patients
options.C: Keeping the room temperature below twenty degrees Celsius
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees

explanation: Raising the bed head keeps oral and stomach secretions from sliding down into the lungs. Simple position changes make a massive difference! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of adding PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure) to a ventilator?

options.A: To keep tiny air sacs in the lungs from collapsing at the end of exhalation
options.B: To force carbon dioxide out of the bloodstream into the lungs faster
options.C: To prevent the patient from waking up during sedation holidays
options.D: To measure the exact strength of the patient's heart contractions

explanation: PEEP acts like a gentle push that keeps the tiny lung air sacs open, making it much easier for the patient to absorb oxygen. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h4)

question: What two measurements are used to calculate cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) in the brain?

options.A: Mean arterial pressure and intracranial pressure
options.B: Systolic blood pressure and respiratory rate
options.C: Heart rate and central venous pressure
options.D: Oxygen saturation and core body temperature

explanation: You find the CPP by taking the mean arterial pressure and subtracting the intracranial pressure. You've got this formula down! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient with a head injury has their brain pressure (ICP) spike every time care is given. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Space out nursing care activities and avoid sudden neck flexion
options.B: Stop all neurological assessments for the remainder of the shift
options.C: Encourage family members to talk loudly to stimulate the patient
options.D: Lower the head of the bed completely flat to rest the patient

explanation: Doing everything at once can overwhelm a sensitive brain. Spacing out tasks and keeping the neck straight helps keep pressure stable. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer feeding patients through the gut (enteral nutrition) rather than through a drip (parenteral nutrition) when possible?

options.A: It requires no special monitoring of blood glucose or laboratory tests
options.B: It helps maintain gut health and prevents bacteria from escaping into the body
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of aspiration or gastrointestinal upset
options.D: It is absorbed directly into the bloodstream without needing digestion

explanation: Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut lining strong and stops bad bacteria from wandering where they shouldn't! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is a very common blood sugar issue caused by severe stress in critically ill patients?
explanation: When the body goes through severe stress or trauma, it releases hormones that often shoot blood sugar levels right up. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) in the ICU?

options.A: To measure the depth of sedation or level of agitation in a patient
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of intravenous pain medication needed
options.C: To assess the risk of pressure ulcer formation over bony prominences
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs are exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide

explanation: The RASS score helps the whole healthcare team figure out if a patient is resting peacefully, too sleepy, or too restless. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why do ICUs often pause a patient's sedative medications for a short time every day?

options.A: To test the electrical activity of the heart muscles under stress
options.B: To allow family members to visit without medical equipment in the way
options.C: To ensure the patient has completely recovered from their primary disease
options.D: To reduce the duration of mechanical ventilation and prevent delirium

explanation: Giving a daily break from sedatives helps patients wake up sooner, get off the breathing machine faster, and stay mentally clear. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is an effective nursing action to prevent blood clots (DVT) in an ICU patient who has to stay in bed?

options.A: Keeping the patient's legs elevated higher than the heart all day
options.B: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent blood thickening
options.C: Applying sequential compression devices to the lower extremities
options.D: Massaging the calf muscles firmly every two hours

explanation: Compression sleeves gently squeeze the legs to keep blood moving smoothly, which stops dangerous clots from forming when patients can't walk. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h8)

question: A patient has a urinary catheter in the ICU. What is the most important step a nurse can take to prevent a catheter-related infection?

options.A: Changing the urinary drainage bag every twelve hours
options.B: Removing the catheter as soon as it is clinically unnecessary
options.C: Irrigating the catheter with sterile saline twice per shift
options.D: Applying antibiotic ointment to the urethral meatus daily

explanation: The longer a catheter stays in, the higher the infection risk. Taking it out the moment it's no longer needed is the best defense! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the main role of the critical care nurse when family and medical teams disagree on life support choices?

options.A: Acting as a patient advocate to uphold their wishes and values
options.B: Directing the family members to leave the unit during discussions
options.C: Making the final legal decision on behalf of the medical team
options.D: Consulting hospital finance departments about treatment costs

explanation: Nurses stand up for the patient's voice, making sure their values and known preferences guide tough care choices. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h9)

question: Why is supporting family members such an important part of critical care nursing?

options.A: Family members are legally required to perform routine nursing care tasks
options.B: Visitors help keep the unit quiet by managing other patients' alarms
options.C: Families experience high levels of stress and trauma during critical illness
options.D: Involving relatives reduces the need for expensive hospital monitoring equipment

explanation: Having a loved one in the ICU is emotionally draining for families. Being kind, clear, and supportive is a core part of caring for them too. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h9)
